item.description: The U.S. Department of Energy accidentally left Vermont off a key energy investment map. This oversight highlights concerns about Vermont's visibility in federal infrastructure plans. Officials and residents are watching closely for any impacts from this omission.

Pittsford could raise about one hundred sixty-four thousand dollars a year with a local option tax on rooms, meals, and alcohol. Town officials are considering asking voters to approve the tax to help pay for infrastructure projects. This could ease property tax burdens for residents if passed.

Gas prices in Vermont have dropped four cents to four dollars thirty-four cents per gallon. Burlington's average price fell nearly three cents to four dollars forty cents. Despite the drop, prices remain more than a dollar higher than last year.

Amtrak ridership in Vermont has jumped forty percent since before the pandemic. The Ethan Allen Express line to New York City has boosted passenger numbers. Vermont is also working to restore rail service to Quebec and will receive nearly four million dollars for its fleet.
